title: Buying a Twingo phase 2: what to check before saying yes
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: A Twingo phase 2 may not cost much to buy, but it can still cost time and many small bills if one neglects the shell, electrical details and coherence of the version.
content:
Phase 2 attracts because it remains simple, light and still affordable. That apparent ease does not remove the need to inspect the car methodically, especially when examples have already lived long lives.

Start with version coherence

Even before the drive, one should check that the car matches what the seller claims: period, trim, equipment and overall state. Small Renaults of this age have often been repaired or mixed across the years.

Correct papers do not prevent incoherence, but they give a first frame. The rest has to be confirmed by the car itself.

Read the shell before the engine

Sills, floors, wheel arches, panel alignment and any trace of corrosion or repair should come before mechanical enthusiasm. A sound small car is worth more than a correct engine inside a weak shell.

This is often the most profitable check. Body problems consume budget and energy very quickly.

Road test and small components

During the test drive, the steering, brakes, gearbox feel, stray noises, simple equipment and cooling all matter. Nothing is very complex, but everything should make sense together.

A good phase 2 is not necessarily perfect. It should above all feel honest, maintained and ready to resume regular use without an endless list of neglected details.
